flashcards.back: Who knows yoga best: devotees of God's personal aspect, or those who worship the impersonal Eternal Being?
The best yogis are steadfast devotees who worship with supreme faith, mind fixed on him as their personal God.
The unmanifest is hard for embodied beings to grasp, so that path is more difficult.
Let mind and intellect dwell on God through meditation and contemplation, and you will reach him.
Practise any spiritual discipline; if not, work for God; if not, give up the fruits of all work.
Scriptural knowledge beats ritual; meditation beats knowledge; renouncing attachment to fruits beats meditation.
One who neither rejoices nor grieves, neither likes nor dislikes, beyond good and evil, and full of devotion.
Faithful devotees with God as their goal who follow, or just sincerely try to develop, these virtues.

flashcards.front: A few marks of a devotee
flashcards.back: Hates no creature, is friendly and compassionate, free of ego and possessiveness, forgiving, content, even-minded.

quiz.text: Whom does Krishna call the best yogis in 12.2?

options.B: Steadfast devotees of his personal form

quiz.why: Worship with supreme faith, mind fixed on him.

quiz.text: Why is worship of the unmanifest harder?

options.B: The unmanifest is hard for humans to grasp

quiz.text: If you cannot fix your mind on God, Krishna says:

options.B: Practise a discipline, or work for him, or give up the fruits

quiz.why: Four ascending levels: each person starts where they can.

quiz.text: In 12.12, what is better than meditation?

options.C: Renouncing attachment to the fruits of work

quiz.text: What follows renunciation of attachment to fruits?
Who is "very dear" to God in 12.20?

options.B: Those who sincerely try to develop these values

quiz.why: Even sincere trying is dear to him.

children.text: Hates no one, kind to all
